course_summary:
ISEN 689 | Special Topics in Healthcare Human-Systems Engineering | Fall 2026
Instructor: Farzan Sasangohar | sasangohar@tamu.edu
Meets: TR 2:20PM-3:35PM | ETB 1013
Grading: Research report [40%], Homework assignments [30%], Reflections [20%], Practicum [10%] — A: 90-100% B: 80-89% C: 70-79% D: 60-69% F: 59% and lower
Topics: Design for X (DfX) methodology, Hierarchical Task Analysis, Digital Prototyping, Usability Testing, Heuristic Evaluation, scoping review, narrative review, systems engineering methods, healthcare human-systems engineering, population-specific criteria (X's), designing a safe and usable healthcare ecosystem, Applications of Human Factors, critical and emergent issues in healthcare, patient safety, human factors and ergonomics (HFE), design and operational problems in healthcare domains, HFE solutions, HFE principles, design problems, role and scope of human factors/ergonomics in healthcare, human factors engineering methods, analysis of healthcare systems, design of healthcare systems, implementation of healthcare systems, evaluation of healthcare systems, emerging topics related to HF/E in healthcare, productivity in healthcare settings, safety in healthcare settings, wellness in healthcare settings, satisfaction in healthcare settings, healthcare applications, detailed case study, background research, application of HF/E, Medical Device Safety, Medication Safety, Digital Health, Mobile Health Technologies, eHealth, Telehealth, Effective Care Collaboration, Healthcare Systems: Critical Care, Healthcare Systems: Emergencies, Resilience in Healthcare, Collaborative Work, Healthcare Workflows, Interruptions, safety culture/climate, special populations, mental health, research project, teamwork, communication skills, research paper, research report proposal, conducting literature reviews, Practicum Presentations
Tools: Canvas, Figma
Prerequisites: ISEN 330 or Approval of Instructor
